Two commands reload during development: aiui dev for a docs site and aiui run --reload for an app.

Run it in the folder that holds aiui.yaml: It builds the site, serves it and opens it in the browser. Save a page, a snippet or aiui.yaml and the site rebuilds and the open tab reloads by itself, at the same scroll position (the URL keeps the #heading). No configuration needed to start. A folder with only a docs/ folder of Markdown files works: the site is built with the defaults and titled after the folder. A broken edit never takes the preview down. The error is printed in the terminal and shown over the page, and the last good build stays up until you save a fix. Warnings from the build (content checks) print once each in the terminal. Production output is untouched. Each build goes to a temporary folder, removed on exit. The few lines of script that listen for rebuilds are added to pages as they are served, so aiui build output never contains them. The preview is served the way aiui serve serves the build: the same routes, cache rules and base path. The tab listens on /__aiui/dev (Server-Sent Events) with a script served from /__aiui/dev.js, so the preview runs under the site's Content Security Policy. It only answers on this machine unless you pass --host; build errors include file paths, so expose it only on a network you trust. Every option is in the CLI reference.

aiui serve --watch rebuilds the site into the output folder on every change in the configuration's folder, without reloading the browser. Use it when you want the built files on disk; aiui dev is the writing loop.
Uvicorn restarts the server when a file in the folder of app.py changes, and the restarted server loads app.py again with the same style, datastore and config.
